facts.summary: Kentucky's minimum wage is $7.25/hour and by statute automatically tracks the federal rate, so it matches the federal floor.
facts.notes: Statute pegs the state rate to the federal minimum and raises it only if the federal rate exceeds it. Verify no 2026 legislative increase took effect (SB 16 proposing $10-$15 was introduced but confirm enactment status).

facts.value: seventh-day premium: time-and-a-half for hours worked on the 7th consecutive day of a workweek
facts.summary: Beyond the federal 40-hour rule, Kentucky requires time-and-a-half for time worked on the seventh day when an employee works all seven days of a workweek.
facts.notes: Otherwise Kentucky follows federal FLSA (time-and-a-half after 40 hrs/week). Seventh-day rule has exceptions (e.g., supervisory employees) and 7th-day premium may be credited against weekly OT owed. No state daily-OT rule and no higher state salary threshold identified.

facts.summary: The Kentucky Civil Rights Act adds smoker/nonsmoker status as a protected class beyond the federal set (race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age 40+, disability).
facts.notes: Statewide statute does not list sexual orientation or gender identity; those are covered only by Executive Order 2020-214 and various local 'Fairness' ordinances, not the KCRA itself. Confirm current EO/local status before relying on SOGI coverage.

facts.summary: Kentucky's anti-discrimination law covers employers with 8 or more employees, a lower threshold than the federal 15 (though disability claims still require 15+).
facts.notes: 8+ employees in each of 20+ calendar weeks in the current or preceding year for most claims; disability discrimination requires 15+ employees, matching federal ADA. Confirmed by Kentucky Commission on Human Rights.

facts.summary: An employment discrimination charge must be filed with the Kentucky Commission on Human Rights within 180 days of the alleged unlawful practice.
facts.notes: 180 days applies to employment, public accommodations, and financial-transaction charges (housing is 365 days). KCHR has a worksharing agreement with the EEOC. Note: a direct court action under the KCRA generally follows the separate civil statute of limitations.

facts.summary: A wage claim under Kentucky's Wage and Hour Act must be commenced within three years after the cause of action accrued.
facts.notes: 2024 HB 320 shortened the KWHA limitations period from five years to three years; confirm the current codified subsection text on the official statute page, which loads as a PDF in some fetchers.

facts.value: next regular payday or within 14 days of separation, whichever is later
facts.summary: On termination or resignation, Kentucky requires final wages by the next regular payday or within 14 days of separation, whichever occurs later.
facts.notes: Applies to both voluntary and involuntary separations. No federal analog requires a specific final-pay deadline.

facts.value: public employees: protected from reprisal for disclosing violations; claim within 90 days
facts.summary: The Kentucky Whistleblower Act protects public (government) employees from reprisal for reporting suspected legal violations, mismanagement, or dangers to public health/safety, with a 90-day window to sue.
facts.notes: This statute covers public employers/employees only; it does not create a general private-sector whistleblower cause of action. Retaliation for filing wage complaints is separately barred under KRS 337, and KCRA retaliation under KRS 344.280. Confirm the 90-day filing period against KRS 61.103.
